question: Which of the following amendment act of the Indian constitution replaced the term "internal disturbance" with "armed rebellion" in the context of a national emergency?
solution:
The correct answer is __**44th Amendment Act, 1978**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The **44th Amendment Act, 1978** replaced the term **"internal disturbance"** with **"armed rebellion"** in Article 352 of the Constitution of India.
 
• This amendment was introduced to restrict the scope of declaring a **national emergency**, ensuring it could not be misused for political purposes.
 
• The term **"internal disturbance"** was considered vague and susceptible to misuse, whereas **"armed rebellion"** is more specific and denotes severe internal conflict involving armed forces.
 
• The change was part of the reforms aimed at safeguarding democratic principles after the misuse of emergency powers during the **1975-77 Emergency** declared under the leadership of then Prime Minister **Indira Gandhi**.
 
• The 44th Amendment Act also introduced other provisions to make it harder to impose a national emergency, such as requiring the written recommendation of the Cabinet before the President could proclaim an emergency.
